conviction_note: The main finding is the 2026-09-21 CEO-appointment release (a primary document). It says Q2 results through mid-September were 'strong ... similar to' Q1, which was $2.12 adjusted EPS ($1.33 GAAP). My own walk lands near $1.8-2.0, against stale and disputed bars of $0.78 and $1.07. So p_up is 63, held below 70 because the statement has been public for a month and the stock fell 6% the day it came out. The bar is disputed, credit gets a reserve build from looser underwriting, and the last two prints in this seasonal slot sold off double digits. abs_move_pct is 12, near the name's 12.8% median: there is no option market, a single Hold analyst and a crowded float. The scaled number (+3.1) and impact_sum (+3.5) agree in sign and size because no lesson pulled them apart.
bar: Disputed. Q2 FY27 (Sep-2026 quarter) consensus EPS is $0.78 with revenue of $140.7M per Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/wrld, read 2026-10-22, which also confirms the 7:30 AM ET pre-open release). A search snippet of Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WRLD/earnings-forecasts, 403 on fetch, snippet_only) gives $1.07 EPS and $140.7M revenue. Last quarter's EPS bar was $0.44 against $2.12 adjusted (https://finviz.com/news/372423/world-acceptance-tops-earnings-forecasts-despite-softer-than-expected-revenue), so the printed consensus is a poor read of what the market expects. print_vs_bar_pct is my ~$1.85 estimate against the higher $1.07 bar. The company gives no numeric guidance.
positioning_check: Short interest was 395,042 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement: 8.5% of the 4.66M shares outstanding, 6.22 days to cover. It has fallen steadily from 507,594 on 2026-07-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/wrld/shortinterest, read 2026-10-22). The free float is much smaller than shares outstanding: the Prescott group holds 28.5% via PGP, Smith 11.9%, and insiders 38% per MarketBeat (13D/A https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/108385/000110465926098328/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml). As a share of float, the short is therefore roughly 14-20%, which is crowded. There is no options market (baseline options.status = no_options_market), so there is no skew. Run-up is -0.41% over 5 days and +0.54% over 20, with the price 23.3% below the 52-week high and ~16% below the post-Q1 close of $204.67.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-21 the company named CFO John Calmes CEO in a release (8-K Ex 99.1) that says the business is 'producing strong results' through the first two and a half months of the second fiscal quarter, 'similar to' Q1. Q1 was $2.12 adjusted / $1.33 GAAP EPS against a $0.44 consensus. My bottom-up Q2 is about $1.8-2.0: revenue ~$141M; provision ~$44-46M, with net charge-offs below last year's $41.1M as the charge-off rate fell to 18.2% from 19.4% in Q1; core G&A ~$72-73M; interest ~$11.6M; ~4.55M diluted shares. That is far above the disputed $0.78/$1.07 Q2 consensus. The year-ago Q2 was a GAAP loss of -$0.38, which included a $3.7M bond-redemption charge.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-24) adjusted EPS of $2.12 against $0.44 gave +13.03%. Q2 FY26 (2025-10-23), a GAAP loss of -$0.38, gave -12.80%. Q3 FY26 (2026-01-27), -$0.19 against $0.78, gave -17.58%. This name pays heavily on the EPS line both ways.
findings.why_not_priced: The statement is public, but the stock fell 6.1% that day (182.14 to 171.09 on 2.3x normal volume) while peer RM was flat (31.39 to 31.50). It has since traded at $166-180, ~16% below the post-Q1 level, which looks more like the internal-CEO news than a strong Q2 being priced. The one listed analyst consensus ($0.78/$1.07) has not moved toward a Q1-like run-rate. If the quarter were priced, the stock would be back near the $190-205 range it held after the Q1 beat.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 8-K exhibit: credit improving, provision -13% y/y, and the release says new-customer lending will increase 'carefully' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108385/000143774926024363/ex_992357.htm). It is the same company but a different document and date. Finding 3 rests on that Q1 document.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-14 the company bought 133,199 shares (~2.9% of the 4,663,180 outstanding) from the Prescott group at $187.69, ~$25.0M, the day after an 8-K authorizing up to $50.0M of repurchases. That cuts the weighted Q2 diluted share count by ~1.4% (fully in Q3). It is funded on the revolver, with debt already $572.8M at 7.8% (+~$0.5M interest a quarter). About $25M of authorization remains.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26 repurchases of 16.5% of shares ($132.4M) did not stop -12.8% and -17.6% reactions on loss quarters. No measured reaction on this line alone.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public in a 13D/A, but a single-analyst EPS bar of $0.78-1.07 is unlikely to carry the share-count cut. The money buys stock 9% above today's $171.67 from the largest holder, so the market may read it as accommodating an exit rather than as value. The size is small for that reason.
findings.independence: 8-K Item 8.01 buyback authorization, 2026-08-13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/108385/000010838526000037/0000108385-26-000037.txt). Same transaction, different filer.

findings.finding: Credit entering Q2 was better than a year ago. At 2026-06-30 the annualized net charge-off rate was 18.2% (19.4% a year earlier), 61+ day delinquency 5.2% (5.4%) and 0-60 day 18.1% (19.2%). Provision was down 13.4% y/y, and new-customer volume was down 40.1% after the box was tightened. Fewer, older-vintage loans should hold Q2 charge-offs below last year's $41.1M (17.1%), when 61+ day delinquency had risen to 5.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27's lower provision drove the $2.12 adjusted EPS and the +13.0% reaction. The rising credit cost in Q2/Q3 FY26 coincided with -12.8% and -17.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it is the Q1 data already reacted to. What is new is the q/q carry-through into a quarter whose consensus ($0.78-1.07) implies credit costs well above the Q1 run-rate. It overlaps finding 1, which covers the quarter as a whole, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The Q2 FY26 8-K gives the comparison base: $41.1M charge-offs and 5.8% 61+ day delinquency (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/108385/000143774925031573/ex_874833.htm). The 2026-09-21 statement (finding 1) points the same way but is a separate document.

findings.finding: Management began 'generally loosening a little bit' of the credit box about a month before the 2026-07-24 call. The Q1 release says it 'expect[s] to carefully increase new customer lending in the coming quarters.' Under CECL, renewed new-customer growth in Q2 builds reserves at the 2026-09-30 quarter-end, ahead of the October-December peak season. New-customer vintages carry the highest losses. Last year a +40.4% new-customer volume quarter took Q2 provision to $49.8M on 4.0% q/q loan growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two growth-season prints with reserve builds and GAAP losses (2025-10-23 and 2026-01-27) sold -12.8% and -17.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar ($0.78-1.07) may already embed a build, and the CEO's 'similar to Q1' comment covers this period. The risk is concentrated in the quarter-end reserve and in what the release says about Q3 growth, which the mid-September comment could not see. The size was cut from -1.5 for the crowded short (lesson 7).
findings.independence: The Q1 FY27 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108385/000143774926024363/ex_992357.htm) carries the same 'increase new customer lending' language. Same company, two documents, one fact, so it is filed once. The transcript is partly garbled per the page.

findings.finding: Short interest was 395,042 shares (8.5% of shares outstanding, roughly 14-20% of the float outside the Prescott group and insiders) with 6.22 days to cover at 2026-09-30, falling from 507,594 on 2026-07-31. Average volume is ~50k shares a day, so a beat meets a crowded short that cannot cover quickly.

findings.finding: Leadership change inside the quarter: the CFO became CEO effective 2026-09-21 ($600k salary, $300k guaranteed FY27 bonus, $500k equity grant). No new CFO was named; the SVP of Accounting became principal financial officer. The prior CEO's exit cost $4.6M in Q1, and this is the new CEO's first call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the announcement day the stock fell 6.1% while RM was flat. There is no earlier print with a new CEO in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The appointment itself is priced (the 9-21 drop). What is not is the new CEO's first strategic framing on the call: a growth push, a CFO hire, or capital-return policy. The direction is unknown, so the size is small with a wide band.
findings.independence: Same 8-K as finding 1's exhibit; this finding uses the Item 5.02 body, not the operating comment.

findings.finding: Revenue is at the bar. Q1 revenue of $139.2M missed $140.8M consensus. The Q2 consensus is $140.7M (two sources agree), while last year's Q2 of $134.5M grown at Q1's +4.8% gives ~$141.0M, with gross loans up only 2.3% y/y at June and the customer base down 1.9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 missed revenue by $1.6M and still rose 13.0% on EPS; revenue has not decided the reaction here.
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue bar is roughly correct, so this is a near-zero item. It is filed because a second revenue miss alongside slowing customer counts is the one line that could make a 'quality of beat' complaint.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 revenue base from the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/108385/000143774925031573/ex_874833.htm). Customer-base -1.9% from the Q1 FY27 8-K exhibit.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The evidence leans positive against a stock that has drifted 16% below its post-Q1 level and fell on the very release that flagged a strong Q2, so the price is not leaning my way and p_up is held at 63 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, 6.2 days to cover, ~14-20% of float): the underwriting-loosening negative cut from -1.5 to -1.0, insider selling from -0.2 to -0.1.

Lesson 6 (disputed EPS bar, $0.78 against $1.07) and lesson 8 (thin coverage with a confirmed company-level statement) push opposite ways on finding 1. Both bars sit far below the Q1-like run-rate, so the size stays at +3.0, print_vs_bar is measured against the higher bar, and p_up stays below 70.
Lesson 8: abs_move_pct raised from 11 to 12, toward the name's 12.8% median, for a one-analyst name with a confirmed unpriced number.

Lessons 1, 2, 4 and 5 left the set standing: the name has paid on the EPS line, the buyback's financing buys stock (capital_return, small), and the unexplained 9-21 drawdown was not filed as evidence.
